title: AEGS Profile
description: A conformance contract: which controls must exist and what evidence must be emitted. A profile never changes a verdict — verdicts come from policy and from the engines. If selecting a profile could tighten or loosen what gets approved, two implementations at the same profile could disagree on outcomes while both claiming conformance, and the profile would have become a second, weaker policy language.

profile.description: The identifier a config names, e.g. `aegs-1`. Lowercase and hyphens so it is safe in a filename, a CLI argument and a JSON key alike.

supersedes.description: The profile version this replaces. A profile history with the superseded versions removed is not a history.

extends.description: A profile this one builds on. Requirements are inherited and may only be tightened — a profile that could relax an inherited requirement would let a higher level be weaker than a lower one.

controls.description: One entry per control this profile has an opinion about. A control absent from the list is OPTIONAL by omission; listing it explicitly as OPTIONAL is clearer and preferred.

control.description: One of the thirteen AEGS controls. A closed set on purpose: a profile requiring a control the standard does not define is a profile nobody can score.

requirement.description: MUST_EXERCISE: runs on every in-scope decision, and the record shows it ran. MUST_RECORD: its output appears in the record when the control exists. OPTIONAL: may be absent entirely, and absence is not a finding.

recordPath.description: Where in a Decision Record the evidence for this control appears, as a slash-separated path — e.g. `assessments/trust`. This is what makes MUST_EXERCISE checkable rather than aspirational: a scorer reads the path and sees whether anything is there.

nonConformant.description: Human-readable statements of what makes a decision non-conformant under this profile, beyond a missing required control. Documentation rather than an executable form — AEGS does not specify a rule language for profiles any more than it does for policy.
